excerpt: Calculate UAE property cash flow after vacancy, operating costs, debt payments and a planned capital reserve.
introduction:
Property cash flow is the money left after the relevant income and expenses actually fall due. It differs from gross rental yield and from a gain on a future sale. Calculate it with the signed lease, the building's charges and the real financing schedule, then test a less favourable year.

The example below shows how rent, expenses and financing come together in one cash-flow calculation.
takeaways: Separate potential rent, vacancy, operating costs, debt service and capital spending.
A positive operating yield can coexist with negative cash flow after loan payments.
Use actual dates and written costs, and stress-test vacancy and repairs.

sections.heading: What is the cash-flow formula?
sections.body:
Start with potential annual rent, subtract a vacancy or non-collection allowance, then subtract owner-paid operating expenses. The result is net operating income. Subtract annual mortgage payments and planned capital spending to estimate cash flow before tax and sale. State exactly which costs are included, so the calculation can be compared with another property.

For example: AED 80,000 potential rent minus AED 5,000 vacancy and AED 20,000 operating expenses gives AED 55,000 net operating income. Minus AED 36,000 debt payments and AED 5,000 planned capital spending leaves AED 14,000 annual cash flow. These are sample numbers.

sections.heading: Use rent you can support with evidence
sections.body:
For an existing tenancy, start with the signed lease and the payment schedule. For a vacant home, seek recent signed leases of similar units, noting the building, area, condition, furnishing and date. An asking rent is not necessarily collected rent. Distinguish an annual rent paid in instalments from cash actually received in each month.

Allow for time between tenants and the possibility of delayed or unpaid rent. The example's AED 5,000 vacancy allowance is a sample assumption, not a UAE average. Ask a local manager for documented comparables and vary the assumption to see how the result changes.

sections.heading: Include operating costs
sections.body:
Request the actual service-charge statement, insurance quote and management agreement. Add owner-paid repairs, maintenance, utilities during vacancy and other recurring costs. If the tenant pays a particular utility or service directly, do not also deduct it from the owner's cash flow. Separate a refundable security deposit held for a tenant from rental income.

For short stays, check current permits and building rules and include cleaning, linen, platform charges, utilities and operator fees. Confirm the fee base and whether it applies to gross bookings or net receipts. Use evidence for the specific strategy and property.

sections.heading: Distinguish finance and capital costs
sections.body:
A mortgage payment commonly includes principal and interest or profit. Both are cash outflows, while principal repayment reduces the outstanding loan; do not treat the whole payment as an operating expense when calculating net operating income. Use the bank's actual schedule and include insurance and fees in the appropriate period.

A planned replacement of furniture, cooling equipment or another major item is a capital cash need. In the example, AED 5,000 is a planning allowance rather than proof that a repair will cost that amount. Record actual spending when it occurs and avoid deducting the same expense twice.

sections.heading: Compare yield and cash on cash
sections.body:
Gross yield is annual rent divided by property price, without operating deductions. Net operating yield is net operating income divided by the chosen cost basis. Cash-on-cash return compares cash flow with the buyer's cash invested, but only if all relevant cash inputs and the period are clearly defined. None of these measures guarantees future income or resale value.

If the worked example used AED 400,000 of the buyer's cash, AED 14,000 divided by AED 400,000 would equal 3.5% before tax and sale. The denominator must include the buyer's actual deposit and purchase expenses; this is not a quoted market return.

sections.heading: Stress-test a difficult year
sections.body:
Increase vacancy, add a repair and change the mortgage rate using the lender's actual reset formula. If the AED 80,000 example loses another AED 10,000 of rent and incurs AED 8,000 of extra repairs, the AED 14,000 cash flow becomes negative AED 4,000 before tax and sale, assuming other items are unchanged. Keep a reserve for such periods.

The [Central Bank’s 2024 financial stability report](https://www.centralbank.ae/media/p2rpafum/cbuae-fsr-report_2025_en.pdf) describes lender affordability requirements. A lender's approval does not remove the owner's need to budget for vacancies, maintenance and changing rates.

sections.heading: Build a monthly calendar
sections.body:
Annual totals can hide a cash shortage when service charges, insurance or loan payments fall before rent is received. Map each due date and receipt on a monthly calendar, including large repairs and any developer instalments. A monthly calendar shows when payments and income fall due across the year.

The [Dubai Land Department tenancy registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/) describes an official Dubai process; verify the current registration requirements for the property and other emirates locally. Use the lease and bank statements to reconcile planned against actual cash.

sections.heading: Account for the purchase and sale
sections.body:
The operating calculation begins after acquisition and does not include the initial price, transfer fees or furnishing. Record those cash outflows separately when measuring total performance. If the apartment is sold, include the sale proceeds, brokerage and other selling costs, and repay any outstanding mortgage. Do not add the entire sale price to annual rent or count repayment of principal twice.

If you intend to compare several years, record when each amount is received or paid and use the same assumptions for each property. A professional can help assess tax treatment and a more detailed return calculation. Keep the basic monthly cash forecast separate from an uncertain future sale price.

sections.heading: Apply the calculation to current homes
sections.body:
Use the [Dubai rental yield guide](/journal/how-to-calculate-net-rental-yield-in-dubai) and [Ajman area guide](/journal/ajman-property-2026) for related context. Browse [Aliyas UAE projects](/projects) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) for current units, then request actual charges, lease evidence and financing terms.

Update the model whenever a quote, vacancy or rate changes. Seek tax or accounting advice where relevant to your circumstances.
